subject: Request: security packet for procurement review — CrimsonHealth MAP-4921
messages:
From: Elena Morales <security@crimsonhealth.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
Cc: Daniel Perez <daniel.perez@crimsonhealth.com>, procurement@crimsonhealth.com
Date: Mon, 10 Nov 2025 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Request: security packet for procurement review — MAP-4921

Hi Stephanie,

We're in final procurement for a Redwood subscription (MAP-4921) and procurement needs the penetration test package to complete the security gating checklist. Specifically we need: a redacted penetration test report, an up-to-date remediation tracker that shows status for any critical/important findings, and a short exec summary we can attach to our vendor risk committee packet.

Timeline: our legal/procurement deadline is 2025-11-20 — acceptance of the package will gate final signatures.

Can you please confirm what you can provide and by when? Also let me know if CrimsonHealth's redaction policy (no vendor internal IPs or internal customer PII) requires anything special.

Thanks,
Elena Morales
Head of Security, CrimsonHealth
security@crimsonhealth.com

[This email was sent on behalf of CrimsonHealth procurement team]

From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
To: Elena Morales <security@crimsonhealth.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 10 Nov 2025 10:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Request: security packet for procurement review — MAP-4921

Elena — thanks for the heads up and the timeline. We're happy to provide a redacted pen test package that meets your procurement gating needs.

Plan:
- I'll coordinate delivery of a redacted pen test report + remediation tracker + 1-page exec summary.
- Internal note: Marcus will confirm redaction scope and any items that require in-person review.
- Target delivery: 2025-11-12 EOD PT so you have time to circulate before the 11/20 procurement cutoff.

Question: Is CrimsonHealth comfortable accepting vendor-redacted reports (no raw logs or full stack diagrams)? If you require third-party validation we can expose the full report under an NDA/in-person review — let us know.

I'll loop in Marcus and Laura for the remediation verification.

Best,
Stephanie Nguyen
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0142

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 11 Nov 2025 08:27:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Request: security packet for procurement review — MAP-4921

Stephanie — quick status update from Security/Platform: we have a 2024 full penetration test (third-party vendor: RedSky Security). Workstreams and attachments I will prepare:

Attachments to include (redacted versions):
- redwood_pen_test_2024_redacted.pdf (executive & technical findings; sensitive infra details removed)
- remediation_tracker_CMH-4921.xlsx (rows for each finding: id, severity, remediation status, remediation_date, verifier)
- exec_summary_pen_test.txt (one page: scope, dates, high-level risk posture)

Redaction notes: we will remove internal IP ranges, hostnames, stack diagrams that could reveal infra layout, and any customer-specific sample data. We'll keep vulnerability IDs, CVE references, and remediation descriptions.

Open items for CrimsonHealth: confirm they will accept vendor-redacted documents. If they need full findings we can provide within a controlled share (NDA + secure link).

Also: one high-severity finding (CVE-2024-2158) shows a code-fix deployed 2025-10-30; we can attach verification evidence (patch diff and a verification screenshot from staging). Reviewer please confirm final verification artifact.

I'll prepare the package and aim to send to Stephanie by 2025-11-12 16:00 PT.

—Marcus
Marcus Lin
Senior Security Engineer, Redwood Inference
marcus_lin@redwood.com

[attachment: remediation_tracker_CMH-4921.xlsx (Excel, 38KB)]

Elena / Daniel — attaching the redacted package for CrimsonHealth procurement review. Per Marcus's note we've redacted infrastructure-specific identifiers but kept CVE details and remediation notes.

Attachments included:
- redwood_pen_test_2024_redacted.pdf (PDF, 2.1MB)
- remediation_tracker_CMH-4921.xlsx (Excel, 38KB)
- exec_summary_pen_test.txt (TXT, 1.2KB)

Quick pointers:
- The high-severity item CVE-2024-2158 was patched and deployed to production on 2025-10-30; evidence is included in the remediation tracker (column: verifier).
- If CrimsonHealth requires the unredacted report we can provide it under an NDA or in-person review; please state preference.

Related links: HubSpot MAP record: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/company/CrimsonHealth (includes SOW and commercial terms). DocuSign SOW link: https://docusign.com/Envelope?e=abcd1234

Next steps: please confirm receipt and let me know if this suffices for procurement gating by 2025-11-20. If you need a short follow-up call, happy to set one up.

Best regards,
Stephanie Nguyen
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
[attachment: redwood_pen_test_2024_redacted.pdf (PDF, 2.1MB)]

From: Elena Morales <security@crimsonhealth.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
Cc: Daniel Perez <daniel.perez@crimsonhealth.com>, procurement@crimsonhealth.com
Date: Tue, 18 Nov 2025 10:06:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Request: security packet for procurement review — MAP-4921

Stephanie — thanks, we received the package and the remediation tracker looks good. A couple quick clarifications before our vendor risk committee meets:

1) For CVE-2024-2158, can you confirm whether the verification in staging was a configuration change or a code patch? Our team needs to record the remediation category in the risk register.
2) Can you send a screenshot of the staging verification (just the verification dashboard view) — we use that as evidence in our audit packet.

If we can get the screenshot and the remediation category by EOD 2025-11-18 we'll mark the item as addressed and proceed to finalize contracting. Acceptance of the redacted package will gate signatures.

Thanks,
Elena
